html:
Workflows — saved requests

A Workflow saves an exact prompt and selected execution settings. Run now starts a fresh Agent task, including normal model reasoning and tool use. Each run has its own conversation and history. Identical inputs do not guarantee identical output.

Choose Save to workflow beside a user prompt, including a historical, text-only or failed request. You can also save an unsent composer draft without sending or clearing it. On mobile, use Conversation options → Save draft to workflow. Open More options → Workflows, the Directory, or /workflows to search, sort, create, edit, run, schedule, view history or delete saved Workflows.

Choose what to save

The editor shows the name, exact editable prompt, execution settings, and three independent context switches. All three start off:

Switch Material copied
Prior chat messages Earlier user messages and assistant answers
Attached inputs Files and attached context available to that request
Previous tool results Earlier result bodies, tool identities and timestamps

Counts, byte sizes and previews help you choose. Earlier context stops before the selected request: its answer, its tool results and subsequent turns are excluded. The prompt is always saved separately, with its own byte count in the editor. A first request with no attachments can therefore show zero optional context, even after a successful run. Unavailable context is labeled separately from empty context; zero optional bytes does not mean the Workflow has no saved prompt. The categories remain independent. A previous tool result is reference material, not proof that a new run has already completed an action.

Selected content is copied into immutable Workflow-owned assets, with checksums. Deleting the original conversation does not delete these copies. Large documents are available through normal context-reading tools. Missing content, integrity failures or storage limits prevent the save instead of silently truncating it. A definition supports up to 16 context documents, each at most 64 MiB; prior-result extraction also observes the receipt store's bounded extraction limits. Turning a category on later requires either its retained owned snapshot or its source data.

Saved execution settings

The Workflow retains the selected Gateway or Gateway group, working directory, behavior, capabilities, permission policy and supported runtime controls. Review these under Execution settings; advanced saved settings are available as JSON. Ordinary parameter values are snapshotted. Credentials remain references handled by existing authentication. Saved settings and captured text are checked for known secret material; binary input copies do not receive exhaustive credential inspection.

Each new manual or scheduled run captures the current Model Configuration, including Main/Helper and optional Vision routing and generation settings. These values are excluded from the saved definition. Once a task is accepted, it retains its own model snapshot through queueing and resume. See Model Configuration.

Historical requests without complete settings require you to explicitly choose and review current settings in the editor. Changes to ordinary global defaults do not rewrite the saved definition. Saved Gateway intent is resolved against the current registry at launch; an unavailable saved target produces an error. Model routing follows the separate per-run capture described above.

Execution-affecting edits create a revision. Accepted tasks keep their original revision. Schedule uses the existing schedule editor and pins the reviewed revision, so later edits do not change that schedule. Deleting a Workflow hides it from the library while preserving revisions needed by existing runs and schedules.

Running and reviewing

Run now uses the saved request and captures current model routing. The API recognizes retries carrying the same submission key, and one Workflow cannot have overlapping open manual/scheduled runs. The browser retains that key on the original Run button after an error; refreshing or rebuilding the library can replace the button and lose the key. If acceptance is uncertain, inspect History and the run conversation before submitting again. Normal queue admission, cancellation, pause/resume, recovery, permissions and live Gateway/account authorization still apply. Saving a Workflow does not save past approvals, browser sessions or completed-step markers.

History shows execution status, revision and a link to the run. Inspect any required interaction or error there. Saved permission settings do not remove mandatory interactions. Workflows use the normal Agent task lifecycle and do not replay a recorded sequence of steps.

API and appearance

The native Recipe skill and /api/agent/recipes namespace use saved_request_v1. Capture identifies a source request and inclusion choices; the server extracts its settings and copies selected content. Edits require expected_revision. Execution requires recipe_revision and an idempotency_key and does not accept replacement runtime context. No conversion of old recorded-step workflows is performed.

See Workflow and recipe architecture for revision ownership, context-file integrity, launch recovery and the distinction between current saved requests and retained recorded-workflow implementations. Browser flow diagrams explain editor drafts, explicit writes, retry limits and library refreshes.

Workflows uses the Schedules layout and shared application fields, switches and dialogs. Appearance preferences, custom fonts, scaling, contrast, light/dark, automatic day/night and System appearance are shared with the rest of the app.
